0.original: Alphinaud draws you close with a whisper.

25.original: Deliver the list of the singer's symptoms and the chunk of meol to Thoarich in the Derelicts.

48.original: (Lady Chai has a very particular sense of beauty, and apparently that extends to how I should dress whilst painting...)

49.original: (But this obsession of hers works in our favor. The time I spend indulging these distractions is time you can use to continue your explorations.)

50.original: (For this excursion, I'd like you to delve into the layer below us, and sniff about the military headquarters. I'm sure the Understory has its own tale to tell...)

51.original: (Now is your chance to squeeze in another round of reconnaissance. Go─I will cover your absence should the Chais become suspicious.)

53.original: You...you're one of the bonded, aren't you? Like me?

54.original: Please, I need your help! My throat, it's... I can't sing anymore...

55.original: I've been making excuses, but it's just not getting any better. If my patron thinks I'm of no use to him, then... <sob>

56.original: I need you to sneak out to the Derelicts and describe my condition to Thoarich.

57.original: Here's a list of symptoms, and a hunk of meol to pay for his medicines... Please, I have no one else to turn to!

58.original: ...You don't know the Derelicts? It's the mess of shacks and ships right outside Joyous Hall.

59.original: That's where the apothecary lives. Or at least, that's what I heard...

60.original: Hee hee! You need medicines? Tonics? Potions?

61.original: Hmmm, a cure for an ailing voice, is it...?

62.original: No, no medicine will cure this. Methinks your songbird has a lump in her throat. It must be cut out, excised, and even then the voice may never heal completely.

63.original: Hee hee, poor little songbird. Will they kick her from the nest, I wonder? Or simply silence her chirps?

64.original: Hoho, your face! You didn't know!? Of the many hopefuls who enter the city, very few are ever seen to leave. Even as corpses...

65.original: Oh, you might see one or two fortunate fools hurled from the balconies, but the rest...? Gone.

66.original: A town of nightmares, it is. Not for this ship's rat, oh no no. I am content to scurry around down here, and nibble on the crumbs which fall from the table.

67.original: This consultation is over! You have my verdict, and I have my meol! Good day!

68.original: All the old hands, they know, oh yes, they know. They just don't like to talk about it. Wouldn't want to upset the status quo, hee hee!

70.original: <sob> ...So that's it? What am I to do if I can't sing...?

71.original: Ah, there you are, my sweet canary. Have you been crying again? Don't tell me your voice is still not on the mend...

72.original: Oh, generous sir, have mercy! I've done all I can, but even the apothecary said...

73.original: ...So you've been suffering all this time?

74.original: I am sorry, my pet. I hadn't realized your affliction was this grave... But you needn't fret! I'll not reward your hours of trilling by casting you out into the street!

76.original: But what use am I if I cannot sing? I fear the day I become more burden to you than treasure...

77.original: Then I shall have a word with Lord Vauthry, and arrange for your ascension.

78.original: In that paradise where resides neither pain nor illness will your song ring out clearly once again.

79.original: ...Or mayhap you think it a step too far?

80.original: No, I... You would do that for me!?

81.original: Of course. Why, I would almost wish to hasten my own ascension, knowing your blessed instrument was waiting there to greet me.

84.original: Sounds too good to be true...

85.original: Ah, you must be a new arrival. Allow me to explain.

86.original: Ah, you must be a new arrival to harbor such doubts. Allow me to allay your suspicions...

87.original: As all know, the sin eaters exist to devour the sinful. But also do they serve to gather the souls of the innocent, and shepherd them unto celestial paradise.

88.original: It is through Lord Vauthry that we learned this truth. It is through Lord Vauthry's grace that the free people of Eulmore are destined to embrace salvation.

89.original: We are blessed to spend our days surrounded by love and merriment, until at last we are called to our final rapture. Even the bonded may find a place within that host, should their patrons deem them worthy.

90.original: Lord Vauthry truly is a great man, isn't he?

91.original: Now if you will excuse us, we must be on our way. May you find eternal salvation for the compassion you have shown my precious canary.

92.original: Oh, dearest, we really should have found you some new gloves.

93.original: Yes, my love, you're probably right...

94.original: 'Tis good to see you back. You were taking so long I began to worry something had happened.

95.original: I've begun sketching an outline for the portrait, but...nay, the Chais appear otherwise occupied. Will you share what your investigations have gleaned thus far?

96.original: So...Lord Vauthry boasts some manner of influence over the sin eaters, does he? That would explain the reverence in which he is held by the citizenry.

97.original: And as for this “ascension” business, I cannot help but be put in mind of that apothecary and his ominous remarks. If so many folk have entered the city over the years, then where do they go...?
